HTTP 304 means "Not Modified." The server sends it in response to a conditional request, one that includes headers like `If-None-Match` (with an ETag) or `If-Modified-Since`, when the requested resource hasn't changed since the version the client already has cached.

With a 304, the server sends no response body. The client should use its cached copy, which saves bandwidth and speeds up page loads. It's a redirection-class (3xx) status, but it doesn't send you to a new URL. It just tells the client to reuse what it already has.
